_notes: Bela Trill Flex - flexible 1D capacitive touch with custom electrode connection, 30 channels, up to 5 touches in CENTROID mode (default DIFF). Address jumper-configurable 0x48-0x4F. Init, as Bela's Trill library (Trill-Linux) for the Flex: CENTROID mode; prescaler 4; scan settings speed 0, 12 bits; a baseline update; noise threshold 123 (0.03 at 12 bits). Poll: up to 5 touches, positions (loc, 0 to 3712 = 29 x 128, the first to the 30th channel; 65535 for no touch) then sizes (size, 0 for no touch; the library scales by 1200 at 12 bits), as 5-element arrays; the dashboard shows them with its touch strip visualizer (vt touchstrip). The prescaler matters: on the bench (Axiom018, 2026-10-23, with the flexible strip) the chip as left after the mode command read 4095 (saturated) on every channel, so no touch was ever seen; prescaler 2 read about 2100-2750 untouched with a finger saturating, 4 about 540-710 with a finger peaking at 1200-1950, and 8 about 0. Bela's library uses DIFF mode for the Flex and finds centroids on the host. Source: the default mode, prescaler and noise threshold are from the defaults table of Bela's Trill library (https://github.com/BelaPlatform/Bela libraries/Trill, LGPL-3.0; also Trill-Linux); only those values and the sensor's documented commands are used, not the library's code (see RaftCore's THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

rsao.note: Trill firmware v2: the first byte is a buffer offset and 0x99 is beyond the 64-byte buffer, so it is NACKed and ignored; reads have no side effects (BelaPlatform/Trill 537ebd6). Firmware v3 isn't public

actions.desc: Noise threshold (counts at 12 bits; 123 is the Trill library's 0.03)
Prescaler (higher reads lower; lower it for more sensitivity, raise it if channels saturate at 4095)
